title: Source endpoint and residue-section continuation of Split-Zero cohomology
programme: Original-zeta arithmetic cohomology and weight-control exploration; complete history precedes coefficient arithmetic; primitive tau is not the recovered integer unit.

results.title: Full-dual analytic injection
results.motivation: Determine whether the whole source functional is retained by the analytic observation.
results.proved: The complete corrected coefficient sequence is injective on the continuous source dual; the actual Hardy domain and its graph are constructed.
results.scope: No Hardy norm is assigned to the entire continuous dual.

results.title: Retained meromorphic endpoint
results.motivation: Keep the endpoint pole and its cover action before taking a quotient.
results.proved: The residue-one source extension is nonsplit before quotient; its full-zero-ideal quotient has a unique equivariant residue section. Endpoint pushout retains the n log n square-zero term.
results.scope: A zero-case receiver sentence omits an explicit conjugation; its zero inference is valid. See the current review and publication notes for the general formula.

results.title: Whole-ideal discrepancy generation
results.motivation: Identify the exact source relations forced by every cover, not a finite collection of observed values.
results.proved: The closed span of the complete cover-discrepancy family is the original full vanishing-jet ideal I in the original source topology.
results.scope: Closure is essential: F0 B is not algebraically equal to I.

results.title: Residue-section and finite-quotient criterion
results.motivation: Calculate precisely what changes under a different residue section.
results.proved: Exact source and strong-dual shears preserve the full meromorphic receiver. For P(0)=1, identity-induced Q to B/PB exists exactly when every root is an actual nontrivial zeta zero with polynomial order no greater than its zero order.
results.scope: Residue-one admissibility by itself does not imply the original-zero quotient criterion.

results.title: Actual Hardy boundary and all-cover reconstruction
results.motivation: Place the actual value boundary into the Hardy receiver and retain the degree defect.
results.proved: The regularized boundary map is injective and trace class on its stated value-sector carrier; all-cover energy and vector reconstructions converge in trace norm without a uniform off-line spectral gap.
results.scope: This value-sector map does not encode higher nilpotent jets as separate Hilbert coordinates and does not acquire the stronger adjoint domain.

results.title: Gaussian whole-divisor energy
results.motivation: Retain the positive reflected energy when antisymmetric traces cancel.
results.proved: The whole-divisor energies, trace and determinant identities retain phases, reflected Gaussians and multiplicities. Current review additionally proves multiplicity-weighted regularized receivers belong to every Schatten S_p for p>0.
results.scope: All-Schatten membership is regularized; no unregularized trace bound or arithmetic cancellation follows.

results.title: Maximal common identity-induced quotient
results.motivation: Construct the exact common quotient when the direct polynomial quotient is incompatible.
results.proved: For r_a=min(ord_a P,ord_a F0) and R(s)=product(1-s/a)^r_a, I+PB=F0B+PB=RB algebraically. Both original quotients map openly and cover-equivariantly onto B/RB, retaining every common jet order.
results.scope: A complete additional proof in the current review companion, not attributed to the historical 647-page body.

results.title: Finite endpoint-section resonance
results.motivation: Compute the full freedom of an equivariant residue section.
results.proved: For one cover n>1 there is one top-jet section parameter at each P-root a with n^(-a)=1. Two multiplicatively independent covers have a unique joint section; common endpoint quotient maps retain the canonical section.
results.scope: Joint uniqueness also holds for non-zeta-root polynomials and therefore is not itself the original-zero compatibility criterion.
